tokens.title: Access tokens
tokens.description: Tokens that let scripts, CI and the SDK call Heimdall. Most people do not need one. Send it in the Authorization: Bearer header to the API at /api/v1.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.confirmRevoke: Revoke {{name}}? Anything using it stops working at once.
tokens.usage: Use it as a bearer token:
tokens.createDescription: The token acts in {{org}} with the role you pick, never more than your own. The scope narrows it further.

runners.title: Workers
runners.description: Computers you own that actually run the agents for {{org}}. Each one only picks up work from comparisons that use its group.
runners.name: Machine
runners.empty: No worker has connected yet. Create a worker token below, then start the worker with it.
runners.tokensDescription: A worker token lets a machine join one group of this organization. Workers get the model keys and secrets each run needs from Model keys and Secrets; without an org key they use their own environment. No machine of your own? Runs use the shared worker when this server offers one.

runners.step1: Save the token on the worker:
runners.installDoc: Install guide for a fresh Linux box

runners.poolInvalid: Group names use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
runners.installLine: Or install on a fresh Linux box in one line:
runners.adminOnly: Workers and worker tokens are managed by admins.
runners.confirmRemove: Remove worker {{name}}? It stops getting work. It joins again if it still has a valid token.

audit.title: Activity log
audit.description: Every change made in {{org}}: who did it, what changed, when and from where.
audit.loadError: Could not load the activity log
audit.readsLogged: Reads of traces, evidence and exports are logged here too, not only changes.
audit.verifyOk: Audit log intact: {{entries}} entries, chain head {{hash}}
audit.verifyLegacy_one: {{count}} older entry was written before the chain existed, so it is counted but not chained.
audit.verifyLegacy_other: {{count}} older entries were written before the chain existed, so they are counted but not chained.
audit.verifyBroken: Audit log changed after it was written: the chain breaks at entry {{seq}}.

org.title: Organization
org.name: Name
org.publicBody: Anyone signed in to this site can read its results and evidence, even if they are not a member. They cannot change anything. People who are not signed in cannot read it; use a share link for them.
org.publicOn: Public: anyone signed in can read
org.ownerOnly: Only owners change visibility or delete the organization.
org.deleteBody: Deletes everything in {{org}}: comparisons, runs, evaluations, agents, benchmarks, keys, webhooks and files. Members lose access at once. This cannot be undone. Audit log entries are kept.
org.leaveBody: You lose access to {{org}} at once. An organization always keeps at least one owner.
org.leaveConfirm: Leave {{org}}? You need a new invitation to come back.
org.retentionBody: Comparisons and their runs older than this are deleted automatically, with their traces and gateway logs. The audit log is kept.
org.retentionCurrentForever: Everything is kept until you delete it.
org.retentionCurrent: Comparisons older than {{count}} days are deleted.
org.deleteDialogBody: Everything in this organization is deleted: comparisons, runs, evaluations, agents, benchmarks, keys, webhooks and files. Every member loses access immediately. This cannot be undone. Audit log entries are kept.
org.deleteOwnerOnly: Only owners can delete the organization.

password.title: Password
password.description: Change the password you sign in with. Your other signed-in sessions end; this one stays signed in. Access tokens keep working.
password.currentHint: Leave empty only if the account has no password yet (signed up with GitHub).
password.done: Password changed. Your other sessions were signed out.

promptLogs.title: Prompt logs
promptLogs.description: Model calls of your runs on the shared worker pass through a gateway that logs them. These logs belong to your organization only: nobody else can see or delete them.
promptLogs.keepOn: The gateway stores the prompt and response text of each model call.
promptLogs.keepOff: The gateway stores token counts, cost and timing only. Traces show no model call text, and fault checks that read request text cannot run.
promptLogs.saveError: Could not save the prompt log setting
promptLogs.loadError: Could not load the prompt log setting
promptLogs.deleteBody: Deletes every gateway log row of this organization now. Saved results and traces are not affected.
promptLogs.deleteConfirm: Delete every prompt log of this organization? This cannot be undone.
promptLogs.deleteError: Could not delete the prompt logs
promptLogs.noGateway: This server has no shared gateway, so it keeps no prompt logs for you. Runs on your own worker log to your own gateway.

experimentActions.regradeHint: Score the saved runs again with the current safety checks. Nothing runs again and the original scores stay.
experimentActions.confirmCancel: Stop {{id}}? Runs already going are saved as stopped; finished runs stay.

regradeDialog.title: Re-score {{id}}
regradeDialog.intro: Scores every saved run again with the current safety checks, as a new re-score. Nothing runs again and the original scores stay.
regradeDialog.lock: Which frozen task list to check against
regradeDialog.lockCurrent: The benchmark's task list as it is now (default; refused if the tasks changed since the comparison started)
regradeDialog.lockFrozen: The frozen task list the comparison started with (use when the benchmark changed since)
regradeDialog.lockPath: Path to the frozen task list (the benchmark lock file) in the project folder
regradeDialog.notePlaceholder: Why you are re-scoring; every report that uses this re-score shows it
regradeDialog.idHint: Default: a new rg_ name. Once the job finishes, the result can use these scores.

problems.badId: Use letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' for the re-score name, starting with a letter or digit.
problems.reservedId: original and reviewed are reserved names; pick another one.
problems.needLock: Give the path of the frozen task list (the benchmark lock file), relative to the project folder.
problems.badLock: The task list path must be relative to the project folder.
problems.longNote: The note is longer than 2000 characters.
